title: ICE bought gloves whose own manual warns they can cause "sudden death"
body: 404 Media got hold of the user manual for the electric shock gloves ICE plans to buy, and the warnings are hard to ignore. The product is called G.L.O.V.E, short for Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter, made by a company named Compliant Technologies. ICE is looking to spend up to $20 million on them. The manual says the shock can "increase the affects that can cause sudden death," including disruptions to heart rhythm, blood pressure, and blood chemistry. That is not a critic's warning - that is the manufacturer describing its own device.

The same manual tells you who should never be shocked with it. Compliant Technologies says not to use the gloves on the elderly, children, or pregnant people. The White House border czar has defended the gloves as a gentler option than deadly force, which is a strange pitch for a tool that comes with a death warning printed inside.
A device sold on the promise that it beats a bullet still carries a body count. ICE just decided that trade is worth $20 million.
